objective: The unattended fleet depends on one file in this repository and nothing checks it. Every Routine that attaches this checkout reads `.claude/settings.json` to learn that it may call its Brain connector without stopping for approval — so a removed prefix, a stray `deny` entry, a trailing comma or a renamed connector does not fail here: it fails hours later, as a fired worker halting at a permission prompt with nobody there to answer it, and it looks from Brain's side like a Routine whose sessions never arrive. The repository has no package.json, no test and no continuous integration, so there is no place that failure could have been caught. Give it one.
expectedOutcome: A change that breaks the settings file is caught here rather than by a stranded worker. `npm test` reads `.claude/settings.json`, fails if it is not valid JSON, fails if either connector prefix the fleet actually uses is missing from `permissions.allow`, and fails if a `deny` or `ask` rule would stop a tool the allow list grants. Continuous integration runs that suite on every push and on every pull request, so the check is a fact about each commit rather than something somebody remembers to run. Nothing about the settings file itself changes, and the repository still contains no application code, no project data and no credentials.
nonGoals: Changing `.claude/settings.json`. It is correct; the point is that nothing proves it stays correct.
Adding a runtime dependency, a framework, a bundler or a linter. Node's own test runner is already in the runtime this repository targets.
Adding application code, project data, credentials or deployment configuration. This repository is deliberately empty of all four and must stay that way.

acceptanceConditions.statement: `npm test` exists and reads the real `.claude/settings.json` from the repository root. It fails when the file is not valid JSON, and the failure names the file rather than reporting a bare parse error.

The suite fails when either connector prefix the fleet uses is missing from `permissions.allow`: `mcp__cloud-brain__*` for the research worker and `mcp__factory-brain__*` for the Software Factory worker. It asserts both are present, and the test proves it is not vacuous by checking a copy of the settings with each prefix removed in turn and requiring the check to reject it.
The suite fails when a `deny` or `ask` rule in the same file would stop a tool the allow list grants, so a rule added later cannot silently take back what the allow list gives.

Continuous integration runs the suite on push and on pull request, on the Node version package.json declares in `engines`, and the job fails when the suite fails. The declared version and the version the job runs are read from the same place rather than written twice.
The repository still contains no application code, no project data, no credentials and no deployment configuration, and README.md describes what the new check does and how to run it.
